CVE-2026-120216.title: fastify vulnerable to Denial of Service via uncaught exception on handlerTimeout with streaming responses
CVE-2026-120216.description: fastify is a web framework for Node.js. In versions 5.8.0 through 5.12.7, when the server is configured with a nonzero handlerTimeout and a route returns a streaming response, a request whose stream has already sent its headers but stays open past the timeout crashes the server. When the timeout fires, Fastify tries to send a new error response on a response that has already started, raising an uncaught ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT that terminates the Node.js process and interrupts any other in-flight requests. An unauthenticated remote client can trigger this with a single request to an affected streaming endpoint, so the impact is availability only, and exploitation requires the non-default handlerTimeout to be set. The default handlerTimeout of 0 is not affected. The issue is fixed in fastify 5.12.8, and users should upgrade to 5.12.8 or later. As a workaround, set handlerTimeout to 0, which disables the affected timeout path.

CVE-2026-130411.title: Code execution through deserialization of pagination cursors in flop
CVE-2026-130411.description:
Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in woylie flop allows a remote attacker to execute code on the server via a crafted pagination cursor.

Flop.Cursor.decode/2 in lib/flop/cursor.ex decodes the after and before parameters with :erlang.binary_to_term/2 in :safe mode. Its check rejects functions, PIDs, ports and references, but it accepts maps, and therefore structs of any module. Flop passes the decoded values to Ecto as query parameters. A cursor value that nests an Ecto.Query.DynamicExpr struct with a DBConnection.Stream struct as its binding fails the Ecto cast. Ecto then inspects the value for the error message, the Inspect implementation enumerates the stream, and DBConnection calls the module, function and arguments in the :log option of the stream.

This issue affects flop: from 0.8.0 before 0.26.7, from 0.27.0 before 0.27.3, from 0.28.0 before 0.28.1, and from 0.29.0 before 0.29.2.

CVE-2026-64855.title: soapbar: verify_envelope_bsp accepts an unauthenticated embedded certificate (signature forgery / authentication bypass)
CVE-2026-64855.description: soapbar is a SOAP library for Python — client, server, and WSDL handling. Prior to version 0.13.0, verify_envelope_bsp() derived its trust anchor from the message it was verifying. It read the X.509 certificate out of the caller-untrusted wsse:BinarySecurityToken, validated only that certificate's not-before / not-after dates, and then verified the signature against that same certificate. There was no CA-chain validation, no issuer/subject allowlist, and no pinning. A successful verify_envelope_bsp() therefore proved only that the envelope was signed by whoever supplied the embedded certificate — never that it was signed by a trusted party. An attacker who mints their own certificate, signs a forged envelope, and embeds that certificate in the token passes verification. CVE-2026-99550.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2: pin owning modules for open debugfs files

The OCFS2 debugfs file operation tables do not set owner. The
full debugfs proxy obtains real_fops with fops_get() at open and
keeps it until final release. Without an owner, this does not acquire
a reference to the module containing the table and its callbacks.
Removing the debugfs entries does not drain retained open files.

An open connected_nodes file can therefore outlive ocfs2_nodemanager
and make full_proxy_release() read real_fops->release from freed
module memory. Heming also reproduced the issue with fs_state and
asked for the other OCFS2 debugfs operation tables to be checked.

Set owner to THIS_MODULE in all eleven explicit debugfs operation
tables: five in ocfs2_nodemanager, four in ocfs2_dlm, and two in
ocfs2. The existing debugfs get/put pair then holds the appropriate
module until final release. Leave the open, read and release callbacks
unchanged.…

CVE-2026-99774.title: xfrm: espintcp: reorder operations within espintcp_init_sk
CVE-2026-99774.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfrm: espintcp: reorder operations within espintcp_init_sk

When enabled on a socket, espintcp sets the socket callbacks to its
own before it has finished setting up its context and published it as
icsk_ulp_data. Any one of those callbacks that gets called before will
dereference a NULL icsk_ulp_data.

Fix this by reording the operations, and add memory barriers to ensure
callers will have a struct espintcp_ctx available. Add a few
WRITE_ONCE/READ_ONCE too while we're there.
